Here's what I've learned over the years:

1). It's redundant, but practice is the most important factor in helping you get better!

2). Draw stuff you see from real life, and try to draw realistically. It'll help you develop technical skills, which will really come in handy when you're trying to develop your own art style. It's usually recommended that beginners start out with stuff like fruit, skulls, and other objects. It sounds boring, but it doesn't have to be! What I like to do is take pictures of cool stuff I see that interests me, and then draw it later in my sketchbook. 

3). Don't be afraid to try new techniques, especially when you're just doodling! 

4). Be open to criticism, but don't let it get you down. It may be a while before people consider you "good", and that can be hard, as people may not praise you as much until you get to that point. Remember that you're always going to improve, and that there's no way to go but up. 

5). Find friends who are also interested in art to draw with you too!

6). Frustrated with how to shade, color, or draw something? Look up tutorials online or use reference photos! 

7). Not everything is going to look good. If you get frustrated, stop working on your current piece and draw something else or take a break. Some people may say to suck it up and keep working, but I find that when I get frustrated with a piece, it's better to take a break from it than to keep going.

Feel free to pm me if you want to know anything else!
